He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]] and the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada Wolf Pack]].{{cite news|first=Chris|last=Murray|title=Born for this: Jalen Harris' path to stardom started early but wasn't easy|url=http://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/born-for-this-jalen-harris-path-to-stardom-started-early-but-wasnt-easy|work=Nevada Sports Net|date=February 7, 2020|access-date=February 23, 2020}} Harris was suspended from the [[National Basketball Association]] for the [[2021–22 NBA season|2021–22 season]] due to a drug violation. ==Early life== Harris was born in [[Dallas]], [[Texas]], the son of Karlin Kennedy and Erion Harris, both of whom played basketball at [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]], and has two younger brothers and a sister. His mother gave birth to him at the age of 19 but returned to the floor at SMU for her junior season and graduated as the Mustangs' all-time leader in points, rebounds, blocks and field-goal percentage. Harris grew up in [[Duncanville, Texas|Duncanville]] and played basketball, [[American football|football]] and [[baseball]]. He gave up football after an injury in middle school, after which he trained with his father to become a high-level basketball player. His father formed the travel team Dallas Heroes around his son in middle school. He attended [[Duncanville High School]] and grew to {{convert|6|ft|3|in|m}} as a sophomore. As a junior, he averaged 15 points, 4 rebounds and 2 assists per game and was named the District 8-6A Offensive Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2015/11/15/boys-basketball-preview-6a-state-champion-plano-west-returns-no-full-time-starters-but-still-boasts-experience/|title=Boys basketball preview: 6A state champion Plano West returns no full-time starters but still boasts experience|last=Jennings|first=Randy|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=November 14, 2015|access-date=February 23, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2015/03/28/class-6a-dallas-area-all-district-boys-basketball-teams/|title=Class 6A Dallas-area all-district boys basketball teams|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=March 27, 2015|access-date=February 23, 2020}} He suffered a broken vertebrae during an [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] event, forcing him to miss half of his senior season. Nevertheless, Harris was again named District 8-6A Offensive Player of the Year as a senior.{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2016/03/26/dallas-area-boys-all-district-teams-find-your-star-player-here/|title=Dallas-area boys all-district teams: Find your star player here|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=March 25, 2016|access-date=February 23, 2020}} He averaged 23 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals per game as a senior and shot 55 percent from the field and 45 percent on three-point attempts. In a game against [[Cedar Hill High School]], Harris scored a career-high 44 points. He was rated as the 16th-best player and the ninth-best guard in Texas in his class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. Harris spurned offers from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] to sign with Louisiana Tech. ==College career== Harris began his collegiate career at [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]]. As a true freshman, he averaged 10.9 points and 3.1 rebounds per game and was named to the [[Conference USA]] All-Freshman team.{{cite web|url=https://www.kolotv.com/content/sports/La-Tech-transfer-Harris-signs-with-Nevada-472418023.html|title=La Tech transfer Harris signs with Nevada|website=KOLOTV.com|date=February 2, 2018|access-date=February 23, 2020}} As a sophomore, Harris led the Bulldogs in scoring with 15.3 points per game while also averaging 4.4 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.1 steals per game, shooting 44.4 percent from behind the arc. He decided to transfer after 11 games. In January 2018, he signed with [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]] over offers from [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]] and [[Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks men's basketball|Stephen F. Austin]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/college/nevada/2018/01/24/wolf-pack-lands-jalen-harris-high-scoring-guard-louisiana-tech/1064080001/|title=Wolf Pack lands high-scoring guard from LaTech|last=Murray|first=Chris|work=[[Reno Gazette-Journal]]|date=January 24, 2018|access-date=February 22, 2020}} Harris chose the Wolf Pack after attending a game against [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]] after being impressed by coach [[Eric Musselman]] and welcoming fans and sat out the [[2018–19 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|2018–19 season]] as a redshirt, during which Nevada finished 29–5. After his redshirt season, coach Musselman left for [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], and Harris entered the transfer portal again the day before the school hired [[Steve Alford]]. Despite receiving interest from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and SMU, Harris decided to stay at Nevada. He missed his second game with his new team with a foot injury and struggled in a game against [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], finishing 3-of-19 with nine points. During an eight-game stretch in January 2020, Harris averaged 27 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game. On February 11, he was named Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week by the [[U.S. Basketball Writers Association]] after scoring a career-high 38 points against [[Air Force Falcons men's basketball|Air Force]] and 32 points against [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Diego State]].{{cite news |last=Ritenhouse |first=Duke |title=Best in the land: Wolf Pack's Jalen Harris named national player of the week |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/2020/02/11/nevada-basketball-wolf-pack-jalen-harris-ncaa-national-player-week/4725906002/ |access-date=February 23, 2020 |work=[[Reno Gazette-Journal]] |date=February 11, 2020}} He had 29 points, a career-high 14 rebounds, five assists and two steals in an 82–79 overtime win against [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] on February 12, becoming the 11th Nevada player to tally at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a game.{{cite news |last=Murray |first=Chris |title=The game that turned Nevada's Jalen Harris into a scoring monster |url=http://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/the-game-that-turned-nevadas-jalen-harris-into-a-scoring-monster |access-date=February 23, 2020 |work=Nevada Sports Net |date=February 14, 2020}} Harris is the first Nevada player since [[Nick Fazekas]] in 2006 to have four or more 30-point games in a season.{{cite news |last=Ritenhouse |first=Duke |title=Nevada basketball: Wolf Pack's Jalen Harris is on a scoring tear ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors (2020–2021)=== On November 18, 2020, Harris was drafted in the second round, 59th overall, in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite news |last=Murray |first=Chris |title=Jalen Harris, selected by Raptors, the 16th draft pick in Wolf Pack history |url=http://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/jalen-harris-selected-by-raptors-the-16th-draft-pick-in-wolf-pack-history |access-date=November 19, 2020 |work=Nevada Sports Net |date=November 19, 2020}} On January 29, 2021, Harris was assigned to the [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web|title=Raptors' Jalen Harris: Shifting to G League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-jalen-harris-shifting-to-g-league/|access-date=April 12, 2021|website=CBS Sports|date=January 29, 2021 }} On May 14, Harris scored a career-high 31 points against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in his hometown of Dallas.{{Cite web |title=Raptors vs Mavericks, May 14, 2021 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202105140DAL.html |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} On July 1, Harris was dismissed and suspended from the NBA for violating terms of the NBA/NBPA ([[National Basketball Players Association]]) anti-drug program. Harris was banned for the [[2021–22 NBA season|2021–22 season]].{{Cite press release|url=https://www.nba.com/news/toronto-raptors-jalen-harris-dismissed-from-nba-for-violating-anti-drug-program|title=Toronto Raptors' Jalen Harris dismissed from NBA for violating Anti-Drug Program|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |date=July 1, 2021 |access-date=July 2, 2021}} He was the first since [[Tyreke Evans]] in 2019 to be banned under the policy.{{cite web |title=Report: Raptors' Jalen Harris banned one year for drug violation |url=https://basketnews.com/news-153232-report-raptors-jalen-harris-banned-one-year-for-drug-violation.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=3 April 2026 |language=en}} ===Vanoli Cremona (2021–2022)=== Harris signed with [[Vanoli Cremona]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] on August 14, 2021.{{cite news Scarborough, Harris recorded 18 points, 4 rebounds and 4 assists, shooting 40 percent from the field (6-of-15), in an 80–70 loss against the [[Montreal Alliance]].{{cite web | Harris tiene 25 años, mide 6’5 y viene de promediar 12.3 PPJ, 3.1 RPJ y 2.5 APJ en 23.7 MPJ con el club Windy City Bulls en la G-League. El canastero viene de anotar 50 puntos, 12 rebotes y 5 asistencias en su último juego de la G-League.|number=1775494314602226038|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=April 3, 2024|access-date=April 3, 2024|language=Spanish}} ===Leones de Ponce (2024)=== On April 3, 2024, Harris signed with the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite web |title=Llega Aleem Ford y Jalen Harris será el segundo importado de los Leones para iniciar la temporada |url=https://leonesponcebsn.com/2024/04/03/llega-aleem-ford-y-jalen-harris-sera-el-segundo-importado-de-los-leones-para-iniciar-la-temporada/ |website=Leones de Ponce |access-date=February 14, 2025 |date=April 3, 2024}} ===Saskatchewan Rattlers (2024)=== On May 9, 2024, Harris signed with the [[Saskatchewan Rattlers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=NBA Experienced guard Harris Signs with the Saskatchewan Rattlers|url=https://www.therattlers.ca/jalenharris-2024|website=CEBL.ca|date=May 9, 2024|access-date=May 9, 2024}} On June 12, 2024, Harris scored 45 points in a 104-93 win over the Hamilton Honey Badgers which was a CEBL record at the time. Harris made 6 of 9 from 3 point range including the game winner in target score time.{{Cite web |last=Sheikh |first=Zulfi |date=June 13, 2024 |title=Jalen Harris sets CEBL record with 45 points in Rattlers 104-93 win over Honey Badgers |url=https://www.cebl.ca/jalen-harris-sets-cebl-record-with-45-points-in-rattlers-104-93-win-over-honey-badgers |url-status=live |access-date=August 6, 2026 |website=CEBL - News}} ===China (2024–2025)=== Harris joined the [[Jiangxi Ganchi]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]] for 2024 season, he averaged 27.5 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.5 assists per game.
